purpose: Current-implementation online KB latency audit; no production algorithm or configuration changes
within_host_execution: One benchmark child process at a time; each case starts a fresh process
read_only_scope: Actual predict_load_samples plus compose, prepared clauses, 128 calls repeated three times. Lattice returns multiple resource targets; Edge currently supplies duration only.
edge_online_scope: 32 real single-clause observations, each with prediction-token preparation, composition, then matched completion and commit. Excludes owner lock contention, persistence, HTTP, and telemetry delivery.
lattice_update_scope: Fork current state, enqueue a real batch, prepare the successor, then activate eligible observations. Single measurement per batch size. Build time is not an end-to-end freshness SLA.
paired_scope: Actual four-backend call-load prediction, common owner lock and background snapshot writer, using prepared clauses. Probe tokens are released with empty completion; no labels are invented. Then 32 real Lattice updates are enqueued together while prediction probes run. Excludes raw parsing, legacy per-clause diagnostics, HTTP, telemetry ingestion, and StateStore checkpointing. Probe cleanup waits are outside prediction latency; this is not a production arrival-process or throughput benchmark.
paired_visibility: Time from enqueue to detecting successor publication, including the probe loop cadence. The following query activates pending rows; published_added_observations must equal 32.
edge_cold_scope: Real online begin/complete replay from an empty graph. The graph adds only exact nodes; this does not represent an offline-built six-order graph. No per-event persistence in this component trial.
guard_interpretation: Experimental stop conditions only, not product limits. A stopped fit supplies no full-model online latency measurement.
limitations: Repeated query calls are not independent workload samples. Update timings and scheduler-dependent contention are single trials, not worst-case guarantees. No full HTTP request or sustained multi-client load acceptance is claimed. The temporary-directory pilot was superseded by these persistent-directory runs. Its measurements are not used in the final comparison.
